chunks: From him, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Uthman ibn Jabla, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

As if I can see the Sufyani or his representative having pitched his camp in your courtyards in Kufa, and his crier calls out: 'Whoever brings the head of [a man from] the Shia of Ali, he shall have a thousand dirhams.' Then a neighbor attacks his neighbor saying: 'He is from them,' and he strikes his neck and takes a thousand dirhams. Indeed, your leadership at that time will not be except for the sons of concubines. And as if I look at the Veiled One. I asked: 'And who is the Veiled One?' He said: 'A man from you who speaks your speech, wears the burqa, conceals you, recognizes you but you do not recognize him, and signals for you one by one. Indeed, he will be but a son of a concubine.'

key_terms.أَوْلَادُ الْبَغَايَا: Sons of concubines, referring to illegitimate lineage, a sign of the corruption of leadership.
key_terms.الصَّفْوَانِيُّ: The Sufyani, a key figure in Shia eschatology who rises before the Mahdi.
key_terms.الْكُوفَة: Kufa, a major city in Iraq central to Shia history and the Sufyani's domain.
key_terms.شِيعَةُ عَلِيٍّ: The Shia of Ali, referring to the followers of Imam Ali (a.s.).
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْبُرْقِعِ: The Veiled One (al-Sakhif), a spy who identifies the Shia during the Sufyani's era.

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'Veiled One' mentioned in the signs of the Sufyani?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) vividly depicts the social fragmentation during the Sufyani's rule in Kufa, where a bounty on Shia heads incites neighbors to betray one another for financial gain, highlighting the erosion of communal trust. He further identifies the 'Veiled One' (al-Sakhif) as a key agent of identification who will single out Shias from the crowd, noting his lineage as 'son of a concubine' to signify his distinct status. This narration underscores the psychological and social trials preceding the reappearance, emphasizing the need for vigilance amidst widespread deception.
